If data are nearly normal, then a 95% confidence interval for the population mean is of the form $\bar X \pm t^\*S/\sqrt{n},$ where $\bar X$ and $S$ are the sample mean and standard deviation, respectively, and $t^\*$ cuts 2.5% of the probability from the upper tail of Student's t distribution with $\nu = n-1$ degrees of freedom. The margin of error is $E =t^\*S/\sqrt{n}$ and in most cases you will find that $n$ is large enough that $t^\* \approx 2.$ Also, for moderately large $n$ $S \approx \sigma,$ the population standard deviation.
